pr.title: Serve getmultipass.dev from site/, redirecting install.sh to the release
pr.head: 331839c8589e9be5737d4dcf60927102c3db592d

summary: multipass's installer is a script that the release workflow publishes as a GitHub release asset. This pull request gives it a short address: https://getmultipass.dev/install.sh. The domain serves no code. A small Vercel site redirects each install path to the matching release asset on GitHub, so the file that runs is always the immutable, attested one.

1. The site. site/ holds one static landing page and a vercel.json of redirects: /install.sh to the newest release, /<tag>/install.sh to that release, and www to the apex.
  2. The guard. .github/scripts/check-site.sh fails any vercel.json that could send an install path anywhere but this repository's releases. CI runs it through tests/site.sh on the real site and on sixteen bad sites.
  3. The deploy. A new Website workflow deploys site/ from main with a locked Vercel CLI and a token that only the production environment holds. Each deploy is promoted explicitly, so it reaches the domain even after a rollback. The job then checks the live redirects with curl, and rolls back when they fail.
This is the top layer of a four-layer stack that carries out the installer plan. The README keeps its checkout install until rollout step 7, when the one-liner goes in.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Vercel: the host that serves getmultipass.dev and its DNS.
  • Redirect: a 3xx answer whose Location header names another URL; curl -L follows it.
  • Dot segment: a . or .. path segment, which curl collapses before sending, so /releases/../../ leaves the repository.
  • production environment: a GitHub Actions environment whose secrets only jobs on main can read.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html: The first review, at eafd7a8, opened four findings and listed three suggestions. The head cfd47d8 answered all seven, and its review was clean, with one wording suggestion on the landing page. This head takes that suggestion, and its incremental review is clean.

groups.title: What the domain serves
groups.kicker: The redirects and the landing page in site/
intro: Vercel serves site/ as a static site with no build step. vercel.json holds three redirects and one header rule, and index.html is the landing page at /.
The install redirects are temporary (307), and they send Cache-Control: no-store, so a new release is live through the domain as soon as GitHub publishes it.

files.note: The redirects: install paths to GitHub releases, and www to the apex.

checks.text: The tag pattern v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+[0-9A-Za-z.-]* cannot match a / or a %, so a request cannot inject a path into the release URL. Checked by reading the pattern.

files.note: The landing page: the one-liner, what multipass is, and installs that avoid the domain.

checks.text: This item now says what a build from source, the prebuilt binary, and the one-liner each trust, matching the plan's README row.

groups.title: The redirect guard and its tests
groups.kicker: check-site.sh, the bad sites it must reject, and the CI step
intro: check-site.sh static reads a site's vercel.json. A redirect whose source ends in install.sh must go under https://github.com/ninjudd/multipass/releases/ with no dot segment, no % at all, and no backslash. Every other redirect must stay on the site. vercel.json must be an object whose redirects are a list with text sources and destinations, and it may set only five keys. The site may hold no file but index.html and vercel.json, so an on-site redirect can reach only the page.
check-site.sh live asks the deployed site for /install.sh and /v0.0.0/install.sh with curl. It checks for a temporary redirect to exactly the expected release URL, with no-store.
tests/site.sh runs the static check on site/, which must pass, and on each of the sixteen directories under tests/site/, which must fail with a named problem.

checks.text: Each fixture differs from site/vercel.json by exactly the defect it is named for. Checked with diff against the real file, and tests/site.sh passes.

files.note: The guard, in two modes: static for a checkout and live for the deployed site.

checks.text: Mixed-case %2E, %252e, %2f, a trailing /.., a lone . segment, and backslashes are all rejected. Checked by running the script on hand-made configs.
A top-level array, a string redirects, an array destination, a numeric source, and a bad entry ahead of a bad redirect are all rejected, while empty redirects pass. Checked by running the script.

A redirect from /v0.1.0/install(\.sh) to an on-site payload.txt, which the previous guard accepted, is now rejected for the file, as are files in subdirectories and hidden files. Only .vercel, which the CLI never uploads, is skipped. Checked by running the script.

files.note: Runs the guard on the real site and on every bad site.
Adds tests/site.sh after tests/install.sh; the cargo steps are unchanged.
A stand-in for a copy of the installer, which the site must never hold.
A script that a redirect could hand to curl | bash, which the guard must find.

groups.title: The deploy workflow and the locked Vercel CLI
groups.kicker: site.yml and the npm lock it installs from
intro: The Website workflow runs on a push to main that touches the site or its tooling, and by hand. Its job runs in the production environment, which admits only main and holds VERCEL_TOKEN, so no pull request can read the token.

The job runs the static guard and installs the CLI with npm ci --ignore-scripts. It records which deployment the domain's alias points at, deploys with --skip-domain, and promotes the new deployment explicitly. It then checks that the alias names the new deployment and runs the live guard. When the promotion or a check fails, it rolls back to the recorded deployment.

files.note: The deploy job, with read-only permissions and checkout pinned by commit SHA.

checks.text: actions/checkout@11d5960a is the commit the v4.4.0 tag names. Checked with gh api on the tag ref.
A Vercel rollback turns off automatic domain assignment until a deployment is promoted. Deploying with --skip-domain and running vercel promote every time works whatever that setting is.
In the locked vercel@65.14.0, promote takes a deployment URL, --yes, and a timeout. Checked by reading the unpacked package's command definitions.

files.note: The Vercel CLI at the exact version 65.14.0, and nothing else.

checks.text: Published 2026-11-09, 17 days before the commit, and the lock's integrity hash matches the registry's. Checked with npm view.

files.note: Marks the lock file as generated so GitHub folds it.
Ignores site/.vercel, which the CLI writes when linking.
